Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

phwstyle 0.3.0

New charts and maps

  • phw_forest() draws your own estimates and intervals by unit, sorted by value. With target, a dashed line marks the target and units are coloured and shaped Higher, Similar or Lower. It calculates nothing.
  • phw_map() joins your data to Welsh boundaries by area code and returns a styled choropleth for Word and PDF. Fills can be continuous, binned or by group, areas with no data are grey, and the boundary attribution is the default caption. It works with facet_wrap(). Area labels are moved apart when ggrepel is installed.
  • phw_epicurve() gains average and average_label, which draw a trailing average of the total count as a black line with its own legend entry. $data gains an average column. Its default date labels now stay within the data, so the last label is no longer cut off.
  • phw_funnel() and phw_spc() gain labels, a named vector that renames zones or signals, and pass ... to their points.

Tables

  • phw_as_summary() gives a table you built yourself, for example with dplyr, the bold variable rows, indented levels and total rows of the built-in summary tables in every renderer.
  • phw_datatable() now styles summary tables like phw_reactable(): bold variable, subtotal and total rows, indented levels, and no paging or sorting by default.
  • phw_reactable() rounds numbers like the other renderers: whole-number columns show no decimals and other numbers show digits (default 1), with thousands separators.

Slides

  • phw_pptx() opens a bundled 16:9 PHW template with Ubuntu text and navy titles. phw_reference_pptx() writes it to a file, like phw_reference_docx().
  • phw_add_slide() gains alt, the screen-reader text for the chart or table, and caption_args. It takes the slide master from the layout, so your own templates work.
  • phw_add_slide() makes charts and tables readable on a slide. Chart text is enlarged 1.5 times (plot_scale), and tables built from a data frame or summary grow to fill the content area (table_fit). A tall table tightens its row spacing so the text can still grow.
  • The Quarto extension gains a phw-pptx format.

phwstyle 0.2.0

Tidyverse-style column arguments

  • Functions that take columns now take them the way dplyr does: unquoted names, c(a, b) for several, and helpers such as starts_with(). For example phw_epicurve(cases, onset, group = organism) and phw_group_table(dat, rows = c(group, type), cols = year). They work in a pipe after dplyr verbs, and accept tibbles. This covers phw_epicurve(), phw_pyramid(), phw_funnel(), phw_spc(), phw_summary_table(), phw_crosstab(), phw_rate_table(), phw_risk_table(), phw_group_table(), phw_flextable_heat(), phw_flextable_groups(), phw_flextable_bars(), phw_reactable(group_col = ), phw_col_bar(), phw_col_heat() and phw_leaflet_polygons().
  • Code that passes column names as strings keeps working, including names held in a variable.
  • phw_leaflet_polygons() labels and popups can be built from columns, e.g. label = paste(name, rate).
  • phwstyle now imports tidyselect. The examples, vignettes and starter documents are written with dplyr and tidyr.

Requirements

  • phwstyle now needs R 4.3 or later (was 4.1). R 4.3 is the oldest version for which Windows users can install, without compiling, versions of ggplot2, flextable, rmarkdown and the other packages phwstyle works with.
  • DESCRIPTION states the oldest version of each optional package that phwstyle works with.

New palettes

  • "extended" now has twelve colours instead of eight: the four "main" colours; then black, green and gold from the NHS Wales logo guidelines and the phw.nhs.wales website; then mint and bright green from the Long-Term Strategy; then a blue, a dark green and a violet chosen to stay distinct from the rest. Every pair stays apart for colour-blind readers. Charts with five or more groups change colour: the fifth to eighth colours were gold, purple, green and grey.
  • "strategy": the colours of the six strategic priorities in the Long-Term Strategy 2023 to 2035, for work reported by priority.
  • "greens": a sequential green palette, from a pale tint to the website green, for scale_*_phw_c(), scale_*_phw_b(), heat tables, maps and plotly colour scales.
  • New colours in phw_colours: mint and green_bright.

Changes to default colours

  • The default palette no longer switches to "accessible" above four groups. Charts with more than four groups now carry on from "main" into "extended" (navy, teal, orange, pink, then black, green, gold and more), so every chart in a report starts with the same colours however many groups it has. Before, a five-group chart was drawn in the accessible palette next to four-group charts in the main one. This applies everywhere groups are coloured: ggplot2 defaults, scale_*_phw_d(), phw_epicurve(), phw_colour_key(), phw_pal(), phw_plotly(), phw_reactable(), phw_flextable_groups() and phw_leaflet_polygons(). Charts with five or more groups that relied on the old switch will change colour. To keep the colour-blind safe palette, switch it on (next item).
  • Accessible colours are now a switch. Turn it on once and every chart, table and widget uses the "accessible" palette, for any number of groups, so one document can be rendered both ways:
    • R Markdown: new palette argument for phw_html_document(), phw_word_document() and phw_pdf_document(), e.g. rmarkdown::render("report.Rmd", output_options = list(palette = "accessible")). The palette is put back when the render finishes.
    • Quarto: phw-palette: accessible in the document’s YAML header.
    • Any route: the environment variable PHWSTYLE_PALETTE=accessible, for switching one render from the command line.
    • use_phw_ggplot(palette = "accessible") and options(phwstyle.palette = "accessible") work as before.
    theme_phw(accessible = TRUE) (larger text, thicker lines) is separate and unchanged: it doesn’t change colours, and the palette switch doesn’t change sizes. See ?phw_default_palette.
  • Colour keys keep a separate copy for the accessible palette, stored as name@accessible with the groups in the same order, so a keyed chart follows the switch and both versions of a report keep their colours between runs. A key used with palette = "accessible" before this version is carried over. phw_key_reset() clears both copies.
  • use_phw_ggplot() now gives the same result on ggplot2 3.5 and 4.0. A layer with no colour of its own (geom_col(), geom_line(), geom_point()…) is navy on both; before, it was navy on 3.5 but grey or near-black on 4.0. Text, reference lines (geom_hline() and friends) and box plot outlines use the PHW text colour, and box plots and violins keep a white fill. Line widths, point sizes and text sizes now match too, so accessible = TRUE thickens lines on ggplot2 3.5 as well.
  • A plot left on the default colours now gets exactly the colours scale_*_phw_d() would give the same number of groups. Past the end of a palette that means spare colours from the other PHW palettes and a warning, instead of blended in-between colours.

Boundaries

  • phw_boundaries("msoa") and phw_boundaries("lsoa") work again. The ONS Open Geography Portal stopped publishing the layers they used, so both now come from DataMapWales (Welsh Government), with the super generalised ONS boundaries as the alternative. MSOAs from DataMapWales have no Welsh names, so name_cy is missing for them.
  • Where a geography is published by more than one source, phw_boundaries() tries the others if the first cannot be reached, and warns which boundaries it returned.
  • An area that a source holds as several rows, such as an LSOA with islands, is returned as one row.
  • phw_boundaries() keeps working when a publisher replaces or withdraws a layer after phwstyle was installed. If none of the layers it lists can be downloaded, it fetches the current list of layers from the phwstyle repository and tries those, and failing that returns boundaries saved from an earlier release, with a warning in both cases. Set options(phwstyle.boundary_update = FALSE) to stop it fetching the list.
  • The list of layers is now checked every week instead of every month. A layer is listed only once a test download works, and a new ONS release is used once its generalised boundaries are published, so the default level of detail is never lost while a release is part way out.

Fixes for older versions of other packages

  • use_phw_ggplot(), and so every phw_*_document() R Markdown format, no longer fails with “Can’t find geom called”histogram”” on ggplot2 older than 4.0. The geom defaults are now set one by one, so a geom that an installed ggplot2 doesn’t have is skipped.
  • On ggplot2 older than 4.0, a plot that mapped a variable to colour or fill and had no scale of its own failed with “argument”n” is missing” after use_phw_ggplot(), which meant most charts in a phw_*_document(). The default scales are now set up correctly there, and continuous and binned defaults use the same blues as on ggplot2 4.0.
  • The R Markdown formats no longer stop a whole render if styling the charts or the flextables fails. The document is rendered and a warning says what was left unstyled and why.
  • phw_gt() works with gt older than 0.11.1, which doesn’t export all_of().
  • phw_page_navbar() works with bslib older than 0.9.0, which has no navbar_options().
  • phw_write_xlsx() no longer fails with “Failed to save workbook” on computers where R names a zip program that isn’t installed.
  • The Quarto phw-typst format works with Quarto 1.5 and 1.6. It failed there with “unexpected argument: spacing”, and top-level headings came out numbered “0.1” and too small.
  • phw_pdf_document() no longer fails on a document with a flextable when the Ubuntu font is not installed on the computer. Tables now use the bundled font, as the rest of the document does.

Other changes

  • The ready-made charts (phw_epicurve(), phw_pyramid(), phw_funnel(), phw_spc()) follow the settings given to use_phw_ggplot(), such as base_size = 14 or accessible = TRUE. Before, they always used the theme_phw() defaults.
  • vignette("phwstyle") has a new section, “How the pieces fit together”: what each function switches on, what you still need to add to a plot after setup, and how your own scales and theme settings take priority.
  • New phw_sec_axis() draws a second measure against its own axis, on linear and log scales, without working out the rescaling by hand. theme_phw() spaces the titles of top and right axes like the bottom and left ones.

phwstyle 0.1.2

  • Resubmission to CRAN. The phw_datatable() example no longer opens a browser when examples are run non-interactively.

phwstyle 0.1.1

  • First CRAN submission. Fixes the notes from the automated CRAN checks on 0.1.0 (wording in DESCRIPTION and links in the README).

phwstyle 0.1.0

  • First release.
  • Brand colours and palettes (phw_colours, phw_pal()), with WCAG contrast helpers. Every palette argument also takes your own colours.
  • A colour-blind safe accessible palette, phw_cvd(), phw_check_colours(), scale_shape_phw() and scale_linetype_phw().
  • Colour keys that keep each group’s colour across charts and reports (phw_colour_key(), scale_*_phw_d(key = ), phw_key_file()).
  • Extension geoms styled automatically (phw_style_extensions()), and multi-plot figures with phw_arrange() and phw_title_grob(). phw_finalise() accepts patchworks and grobs.
  • Summary tables for reports and epidemiology (phw_summary_table(), phw_crosstab(), phw_rate_table(), phw_risk_table(), phw_group_table() for nested row and column groups with group, subgroup and table totals), rendered by phw_flextable() and phw_reactable(), plus column formats (phw_flextable_bars(), phw_col_bar(), phw_col_heat(), phw_col_rag()).
  • phw_plotly() styles every plotly chart type; phw_plotly_colorscale().
  • Public health charts: phw_epicurve(), phw_pyramid(), phw_funnel() and phw_spc().
  • More outputs: gt (phw_gt(), phw_gt_theme()), gtsummary (use_phw_gtsummary()), DT (phw_datatable()), leaflet (phw_leaflet(), phw_leaflet_polygons(), phw_leaflet_palette()), Excel (phw_write_xlsx()) and PowerPoint (phw_pptx(), phw_add_slide()).
  • phw_boundaries() downloads and caches boundaries for 13 Welsh geographies from the ONS Open Geography Portal and DataMapWales, including health boards and GP clusters; phw_boundary_levels() lists them.
  • phw_setup_check() lists missing fonts, packages and tools and offers to install them.
  • Bundled Ubuntu font with Arial fallback (phw_font(), phw_install_fonts()).
  • ggplot2 theme and scales (theme_phw(), theme_phw_map(), scale_*_phw_*(), use_phw_ggplot(), phw_finalise(), phw_save()).
  • Tables and widgets: phw_flextable(), phw_flextable_heat(), phw_reactable(), phw_plotly().
  • Shiny: phw_bs_theme(), phw_header(), phw_page_navbar().
  • R Markdown formats: phw_html_document(), phw_word_document(), phw_pdf_document().
  • Quarto extension with HTML, Word, Typst, LaTeX PDF, revealjs and dashboard formats (use_phw_quarto()).
  • Captions and dates (phw_caption(), phw_date()), with every word changeable.
